name: Werewolf
body:
Werewolves are shape-changing creatures often lurking on the fringes of the wilderness, perpetually oscillating between their humanoid form and that of menacing wolves. These beings are usually indistinguishable from ordinary people, bearing a dark secret hidden within their seemingly mundane exteriors. With the rise of the full moon, they undergo a transformation that sees them adopt features reminiscent of wolves, including fur, sharp claws, and elongated snouts. Within the shadowed bounds of thick forests, mist-enshrouded moors, or even hidden recesses in teeming cities, these lycanthropes (the most common of all werebeasts, including other type of shapechangers like werebears, wereboars, wererats and weretigers) make their homes, creating a life that perfectly blends stealth and savagery, civilization and wilderness. Werewolves often establish tight-knit packs that navigate through treacherous terrains and engage in nocturnal hunts. Others elect solitude, bearing their curse in silence, wishing to shield others from the rage that bubbles within them during their (often involuntary) transformations. Some become even capable of controlling their shapechanging abilities, turning their curse into a blessing. Despite their formidable physical abilities, heightened senses, and remarkable healing capabilities, werewolves are not without their vulnerabilities. Silvered weapons prove particularly effective against them.

The existence of werewolves is often marked by psychological and emotional turmoil, as they teeter on the edge of humanity and beastliness. For this reason, they might even be found serving sinister masters in foreboding castles, carrying out the bidding of these dark lords, or perhaps seeking to undermine their rule, providing unsuspecting adventurers with unlikely allies in a land overshadowed by perennial gloom and terror.

Habitat

Werewolves inhabit various environments, from dense forests and mist-shrouded moors to hidden enclaves within bustling cities. Whether in natural dens or hidden urban lairs, werewolves create sanctuaries marked by the scent of the wild, often decorated with trophies from their hunts.

Strengths

Werewolves possess heightened senses, incredible strength, and rapid healing abilities, making them formidable foes. Both in their wolf or hybrid forms, they are blessed with an enhanced speed and can communicate with wolves and dire wolves, establishing their dominance as alphas amongst their packs. Additionally, they have an innate resistance to damage from non-magical weapons that aren’t silvered. Their bite can transmit their lycanthropic curse, turning victims into werewolves under the light of the full moon.

Weaknesses

Despite their powers, werewolves are susceptible to silvered weapons, which can harm them as normal weapons do to other creatures. They might also struggle with their dual nature, torn between their humanoid sensibilities and the savage instincts of a wolf.

About the Curse

Creatures transformed into werewolves after a bite undergo dramatic changes. The process of transforming in a werewolf is extremely dangerous, and many that experience it could descend into madness or sometimes even die. During each full moon, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or succumb to the beast within, losing control and acting on primal instincts. During this time, they can’t revert to their humanoid or hybrid form, and they may attack their allies or innocent bystanders as they experience a complete loss of control.

Werewolf Traits

Werewolves are formidable creatures that bear the curse (or gift) of lycanthropy. Standing taller and more robust than their humanoid counterparts, werewolves blend the acute senses and primal strength of wolves with the adaptability and the versatility of humanoids. Navigating through a life shadowed by their dual nature, werewolves often grapple with acceptance and identity, living on the fringes of society or in tight-knit packs hidden from the world. While playing as a Werewolf, you gain the following racial traits:

Ability Score Increase. Your Strength score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 1.
Age. Werewolves mature at the same rate as their humanoid counterparts and have a lifespan similar to that of their original race, although some believe the curse can extend their lives.
Alignment. Werewolves tend toward chaotic alignments due to the wild, untamable power that the curse imparts upon them. They range widely in alignment, though, depending on how they cope with their affliction.
Size. Werewolves in their humanoid form maintain the size of their original race. While in their wolf or hybrid form, they are often larger and more imposing, typically standing between 7 and 9 feet tall and weighing around 200 pounds. Your size is medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet. In your wolf or hybrid form, your speed increases to 35 feet instead.
Senses. Darkvision. The curse sharpens your senses, granting you darkvision. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Special Senses. Keen Hearing and Smell. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and any one other language of your choice. In wolf or hybrid form, you can understand but not speak these languages.
Lycanthropic Resilience. You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened. Additionally, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from attacks made with weapons that are not silvered. While in your humanoid form, you also gain advantage on saving throws against being charmed, as your heightened self-control enhances your resistance to external influences.
Shapechanger. As an action, you can transform into a wolf or hybrid form, or back into your humanoid form. Your statistics are the same in each form, with the exception of your speed, as noted above. You revert to your humanoid form if you die.
Attacks. Bite. In your wolf or hybrid form, you can use your fangs to make an unarmed strike as a bonus action. If you hit with your bite, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier. If the target is a humanoid, it must also succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be cursed with werewolf lycanthropy.
Unstable Transformation. The physical and mental toll of transformation can leave you weakened, reflecting the strain it puts on your body and psyche. After you revert from your wolf or hybrid form to your humanoid form, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or suffer one level of exhaustion. Additionally, on each night of a full moon at midnight, you must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be forcibly transformed into your wolf form for 8 hours. During this period, you lose control of your character, who acts wildly, attacking every creature in sight and embarking on a frenetic hunt. After this involuntary transformation ends, you suffer a level of exhaustion.
Becoming a Werewolf

Becoming a lycanthrope, or specifically a werewolf, can happen through various circumstances, and it can either correspond to a blessing or a curse.

Some examples are detailed below.

1. Lycanthrope Bite: The most common way to become a werewolf is by being bitten by another werewolf. The curse is transmitted through their bite, turning the victim into a werewolf during the next full moon.
2. Bloodline: Some individuals are born with the curse because it runs in their bloodline. In these cases, the curse may possibly manifest later in life or under specific conditions set by the Gamemaster.
3. Cursed Object: Coming into contact with a cursed object could sometimes turn a person into a werewolf. These objects are often tied to the moon or to wolves, carrying the lycanthropic curse for this reason.
4. Dark Ritual: Engaging in or being the subject of a dark and ancient ritual connected to the moon or wolves can result in lycanthropy. These rituals often involve the presence of werewolves or their spirits.
5. Divine or Infernal Intervention: Sometimes, deities or devils may bestow (or inflict) lycanthropy upon individuals, either as a blessing, a curse, or a test.
6. Dark Pact: A person might forge a pact with the spirit of a werewolf or a deity. This mystical agreement grants them the powers of a werewolf.
7. Voluntary Transformation: In rare cases, individuals might willingly seek out lycanthropy, undergoing specific, often dangerous processes to acquire the curse and its associated powers.
8. Accidental Transformation: In some cases, individuals might unknowingly or accidentally trigger their transformation into a werewolf, perhaps due to their latent lycanthropic genes or exposure to powerful magic.
Turning into a Werewolf

The process of transformation into a werewolf after a bite is violent and painful, with the afflicted individual’s body undergoing rapid changes during the next full moon, including the growth of fur, elongation of teeth into fearsome fangs, and reshaping of the physique into a wolf-like body. For those newly cursed, the transformation is often accompanied by a complete loss of self-control, with the individual succumbing to a primal, ferocious mentality driven only by the need to hunt and survive. It’s during this initial stage that many do not survive. The stress on the body and mind is overwhelming, and without proper guidance or support, the freshly turned werewolf may perish, either due to the intensity of the transformation or through conflict with other creatures. However, some individuals manage to endure and eventually thrive with their newfound powers through their strength of will. While daunting, lycanthropy is considered by many a dark blessing. Those who survive the initial phases of the transformation find themselves imbued with heightened senses and increased physical strength. With time and practice, some werewolves even learn to wield their transformation voluntarily, utilizing their powers at their advantage.

Being Affected by Lycanthropy

Provided below are some guidelines regarding characters who are affected by the curse of lycanthropy after contact with some powerful force or being bitten by another lycanthrope.

Removing the Curse

Removing the curse of lycanthropy can be done through a remove curse spell or similar magic, but the spell must be cast within 24 hours after being exposed to lycanthropy. Alternatively, a ritual, quest, or divine intervention may be required at the GM’s discretion.

Lycanthropy and Racial Traits

If a character is affected by the curse of lycanthropy and the curse is not removed in the first 24 hours, the character loses all racial traits and abilities from their original race and adopts those of a werewolf. If the character has any feats that require to belong to a specific race, they may select one feat of their choice, including one of the werewolf features included here. At the GM’s discretion, it may take a while to gain one of the werewolf’s features, as the character begins to adapt to their new nature. If the curse is removed afterwards, the character regains their original racial traits and abilities, losing those related to the werewolf lineage.

A character recently affected by the curse of lycanthropy can’t control their transformation until the first full moon, during which they will have to resist losing control of their actions and manage to survive the night. For this reason, the character can’t use their Shapechanger trait until the prerequisites are met, as detailed in the following paragraphs.

A character that dies after being exposed to lycanthropy retains the curse even after being resurrected.

The First Transformation

Upon being cursed with lycanthropy, the afflicted individual must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw at the onset of the next full moon. Failing this save results in an immediate and uncontrollable transformation into a werewolf for the next 8 hours. During this period, the player loses the control of their character, who acts wildly, attacking every creature in sight and embarking on a frenetic hunt. When this transformation ends, the character suffers one level of exhaustion, and they must made a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, 18 gaining additional levels of exhaustion on a failed save, as detailed in the table below. From this moment, the character gains the ability to use their Shapechanger trait, but with some restrictions (as detailed in the following paragraph).

Consequences following the First Transformation
Total Levels of Exhaustion	Result
1	18+
2	15-17
3	12-14
4	9-11
5	6-8
6	5 or less
Subsequent Transformations

For the subsequent transformations after the first (whether voluntary or not), a character must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw to avoid losing control. On a failed save, the character acts wildly and aggressively under the GM’s control for the next 8 hours. Each success lowers the DC by 2, up to a minimum DC of 10.

After you’ve succeeded on three saves in a row to resist losing control, you have learned to harness your lycanthropic nature. You no longer need to make saving throws to resist going wild while transforming (except for those you would normally do during full moon), and you gain the ability to transform at will. From this time, you gain access to your Shapechanger trait, as detailed in the Werewolf Traits section.
